questions.question: A unit five-year endowment insurance pays immediately on death before year 5 and at year 5 on survival. What happens if the insured survives beyond year 5?
options: One unit is paid only at the later death.
No benefit is paid under this contract.
One unit is paid at year 5.
One unit is paid at year 5 and again at death.

questions.question: For immediate-settlement endowment insurance, let $T\ge0$ be future lifetime, $n>0$ maturity in years and $v=(1+i)^{-1}$ the annual discount factor, with $i>-1$. Which present-value formula for the single unit benefit is valid for every admissible $T,n,i$?
A unit endowment insurance has maturity $n=4$ years and immediate death settlement. The future lifetime is exactly $T=4$ years. With annual discount factor $v=0.9$, what is the total present value?

Let $T\ge0$ have an absolutely continuous lifetime distribution, $n>0$ be maturity and $v>0$ the annual discount factor. Define $D=v^T\mathbf1_{\{T<n\}}$ and $M=v^n\mathbf1_{\{T\ge n\}}$, where $\mathbf1$ is an event indicator. Which identity for the unit endowment value $Z$ holds for every such lifetime distribution and all admissible $n,v$?

For a unit endowment, let $D$ and $M$ be the discounted death-before-maturity and survival-to-maturity components. Suppose both events have positive probability, and the component means are finite and positive. Their product is zero for every lifetime. What follows about $\operatorname{Cov}(D,M)$?
options: It is zero because the payment events are disjoint.
It is positive because both components are benefits.
It is negative because it equals $-E[D]E[M]$.
It equals $E[D]E[M]$ because the product is zero.

questions.question: A four-year endowment pays a benefit of 1000 immediately on death before maturity, or at year 4 on survival. The annual discount factor is $v=0.8$, and death occurs at $T=1.5$ years. What is the realised present value?

On a common valuation basis, the unit four-year term-insurance APV is 0.18 and the unit four-year pure-endowment APV is 0.62. Both use the same settlement conventions as a unit four-year endowment. What is the endowment APV?
A unit endowment pays once by maturity $n=6$ years. Its future lifetime has an arbitrary distribution, and the interest rate is zero. What are its APV and present-value variance?
options: APV equal to survival probability and variance greater than zero.
APV 1 and variance equal to death probability times survival probability.
APV equal to death probability and variance 0.

questions.question: A three-year endowment pays 2000 immediately on death before year 3 or at year 3 otherwise. Future lifetime $T$ equals 1 year with probability 0.4 and 5 years with probability 0.6. The annual discount factor is $v=0.9$. What is its APV?

For a unit immediate-settlement endowment, let $T\ge0$ be future lifetime, $n>0$ maturity and $v>0$ the annual discount factor. Its value is $Z=v^T\mathbf1_{\{T<n\}}+v^n\mathbf1_{\{T\ge n\}}$. Which identity for $E[Z^2]$ holds for every admissible lifetime law and all such $n,v$?

Fix the lifetime $T\ge0$ and annual discount factor $0<v<1$. For immediate unit endowments write $Z_n=v^{\min(T,n)}$ for maturity $n>0$. If maturity is increased from $n_1$ to $n_2>n_1$, which statement holds for every lifetime?
options: The direction depends only on whether death occurs before $n_2$.

questions.question: Let $T\ge0$ range over all possible future lifetimes, $n>0$ be maturity and $0<v<1$ the annual discount factor. What is the smallest closed interval containing every value of the immediate unit endowment $Z=v^{\min(T,n)}$?

For the same lifetime distribution and maturity $n>0$, two immediate unit endowments use annual discount factors $0<v_1<v_2<1$. Assume $P(T>0)>0$, where $T\ge0$ is future lifetime. How do their APVs compare?
options: The APVs agree because both contracts certainly pay.
The APV at $v_1$ is strictly larger.
Only the maturity component changes; the total direction is undetermined.
The APV at $v_1$ is strictly smaller.

questions.question: The discounted death and maturity components $D,M$ of a unit endowment have means 0.2 and 0.5 and variances 0.08 and 0.09. Their product is always zero. What is $\operatorname{Var}(D+M)$?
options: $0.17$: the supplied component moments form a valid basis.
$0.37$: the supplied component moments form a valid basis.
$0.07$: the supplied component moments form a valid basis.

questions.question: A unit endowment has immediate death settlement and maturity 1 year. Future lifetime $T$ is uniform on $[0,2]$, with density $1/2$ there. Discounting is $\mathrm{e}^{-t}$ at time $t$ years. What is its APV?

A unit four-year endowment uses annual discount factor $v=0.9$. Its APV is 0.75, and the matching death-before-maturity component has APV 0.30. Let $p$ be the probability of survival to maturity; assume no death exactly at year 4. What is $p$?

For an immediate unit endowment, let $n>0$ be maturity, $0<v<1$ the annual discount factor and $T\ge0$ an arbitrary future lifetime. Observing its present value $Z=v^{\min(T,n)}$, what can be inferred when $Z=v^n$?
options: $T=n$, so death occurred exactly at maturity.
$T>n$, so death exactly at maturity is excluded.
$T\ge n$, but the exact lifetime is not identified.
$T\le n$, but the exact lifetime is not identified.

questions.question: For a unit endowment with finite maturity and a positive discount factor, define $D$ as its discounted death-before-maturity payment and $M$ as its complementary maturity payment. When is $\operatorname{Cov}(D,M)=0$?
options: Exactly when the two payment events have equal probabilities.
Exactly when the interest rate is zero.
Exactly when the two payment times have the same discount factor.
Exactly when one of the two payment events has probability zero.

questions.question: A unit one-year endowment pays at the end of the year of death if death occurs before maturity, or at maturity otherwise. The annual discount factor is $v=0.8$, the probability of death before year 1 is 0.25, and death exactly at year 1 has probability zero. Let $D,M$ be the discounted death and maturity components. Which pair equals $\operatorname{Var}(D+M)$ and $\operatorname{Cov}(D,M)$?

A unit four-year endowment settles deaths immediately and otherwise pays at year 4. The discount factor is $v=1/2$. Future lifetime $T$ satisfies $P(T<4)=0.4$; conditional on $T<4$, it lies in $[1,2]$. All remaining lifetimes exceed 4. With no other lifetime information, what is the sharp interval for its APV?
